source: MAFF / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), Royal Government of Cambodia — ខ្សែសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំស្វាយចន្ទីនៅកម្ពុជា (Cashew Value Chain Study in Cambodia), field survey report (250 household respondents across major cashew-growing provinces), 2017, 57pp
text:
Household-level land, yield, and income data from the 2017 MAFF cashew value chain survey (n=250 households).

Land holdings: essentially all surveyed households (100%) had at least one land plot (average 2.27 ha), 40% had a second plot (average 2.00 ha), and 9% had a third plot (average 2.28 ha); average total household landholding was about 3.28 ha (range roughly 0.08-25 ha).

On average, households planted cashew on about 2.4-3.3 ha of their land. Reported cashew tree ages ranged widely (roughly 5-51 years), and farmers' own cashew-growing experience averaged around 10 years.

Reported fresh cashew nut yield varied widely across households, with the source citing a wide low-to-high range and an approximate average yield in the range of a few hundred kilograms per hectare; exact minimum/maximum figures in the source table were difficult to confirm with full certainty from the scanned image and should be treated as approximate.

Household income from cashew: annual income from selling fresh cashew nut varied enormously across households (from very small amounts up to over 100 million riel for the largest producers), with an average household income cited at around 10 million riel per year from cashew sales. After deducting average maintenance and harvest costs (cited at roughly 3 million riel/household/year), average net profit was estimated at roughly 7.5 million riel per household per year.

Households averaged about 8 members, with an average of about 4-5 working-age (able-bodied) members contributing labor to farm activities.
caveat: Some specific figures in this source (percentages, price points, yield ranges) were transcribed from a scanned document at a resolution where certain digits were hard to confirm with full pixel-level certainty. Figures are reported as best-effort readings of the source; anyone using exact numbers for decisions should verify against the original report where possible.
